symbols.name: X
symbols.def: The binary treatment-assignment path; set \(X_s=0\) for \(s\le 0\) when it enters the response equation.

symbols.name: D
symbols.def: A candidate finite-horizon assignment law for \(X\).

symbols.name: m
symbols.role: half-edge count in the mirrored construction

symbols.name: Xinf
symbols.def: The bi-infinite treatment path used for stationary designs.

symbols.name: Pinf
symbols.def: A candidate law for the bi-infinite assignment path.

symbols.name: W
symbols.def: One random affine Boolean block in the Golay construction.

symbols.name: Phi
symbols.role: degree-two monomial lift whose covariance is fourth order

symbols.name: rhoRS
symbols.def: The control-to-treatment transition probability in a stationary random-switch law.

symbols.name: gammaRS
symbols.def: The treatment-to-control transition probability in a stationary random-switch law.

symbols.name: DesignRS
symbols.def: The stationary homogeneous two-state random-switch law class of Guo and Liang, recoded to signs.

assumptions.condition: The pair \((g,e)\) is fixed before \(X\) is randomized.

standard.name: Design-based fixed potential outcomes with an oblivious disturbance

assumptions.condition: \(X_s=0\) for every integer \(s\le 0\) in the response equation.

novel.justification: A single energy budget is realistic when coefficient magnitude and deterministic drift are alternative sources of misspecification calibrated on one physical response scale; it also permits either source to dominate without imposing a stochastic disturbance law.
Any implementable base schedule can be multiplied by one fair global sign, so the condition is operationally costless and corresponds to relabeling treatment and control for the entire trial.

standard.name: Pairwise moment balance, weaker than independent Rademacher toggling

assumptions.condition: The law \(D\) of \(X\) is the stationary homogeneous two-state Markov law with transition matrix \(\begin{psmallmatrix}1-\rho_{\mathrm{RS}}&\rho_{\mathrm{RS}}\\\gamma_{\mathrm{RS}}&1-\gamma_{\mathrm{RS}}\end{psmallmatrix}\) on the ordered states \((-1,1)\) and \(\Pr_D(X_1=1)=\rho_{\mathrm{RS}}/(\rho_{\mathrm{RS}}+\gamma_{\mathrm{RS}})\), with this probability defined as \(1/2\) when \(\rho_{\mathrm{RS}}=\gamma_{\mathrm{RS}}=0\).

standard.name: Stationary homogeneous random-switch assignment, recoded from \(\{0,1\}\) to \(\{-1,1\}\)

assumptions.condition: The law \(P_{\infty}\) is invariant under every integer shift.

novel.justification: Independent fair signs attached to successive finite blocks produce this property exactly, so it is implementable by a finite-state randomizer.

definitions.name: Legal finite assignment laws
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak D_T=\{D\in\Delta(\{-1,+1\}^T):D(B)=D(-B)\ \text{for every }B,\ \mathbb E_D[X_sX_t]=0\ \text{for every }1\le s<t\le T\}\).

definitions.name: Independent Rademacher benchmark
definitions.construction: \(D_T^{\mathrm{iid}}\) is the law under which \(X_1,\ldots,X_T\) are mutually independent and each is uniform on \(\{-1,+1\}\).

definitions.name: Guo--Liang stationary random-switch class
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak D_T^{\mathrm{RS}}=\{D\in\Delta(\{-1,+1\}^T):\text{there exist }\rho_{\mathrm{RS}},\gamma_{\mathrm{RS}}\in[0,1]\text{ for which }D\text{ is the stationary homogeneous two-state Markov law specified by the random-switch condition}\}\).

definitions.name: Quadratic and linear error coefficients
definitions.construction: \(u_T(X)=A(X)^{\top}A(X)\Gamma_T^{-1}q-q\), \(v_T(X)=A(X)\Gamma_T^{-1}q\), and \((F_{T,q})_{t,s}=q_{t-s}/(T-(t-s))\) when \(0\le t-s<K\), with zero otherwise; hence \(v_T(X)=F_{T,q}X\).

definitions.name: Normalized worst-case MSE and minimax value
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal R_T(D)=T\sup_{(g,e)\in\mathcal H_T}\mathbb E_D[(\widehat\tau-\tau)^2]\) and \(V_{T,K}(q;R_g,R_e)=\inf_{D\in\mathfrak D_T}\mathcal R_T(D)\).

definitions.name: Lag-one parity and threshold objects
definitions.construction: \(S_T(X)=\sum_{t=1}^{T-1}X_tX_{t+1}\), \(a_T=1\) when \(T\) is even and \(a_T=2\) when \(T\) is odd, and \(r_T=T R_e^2/R_g^2\).

definitions.name: Mirrored-edge-sign assignment law
definitions.construction: Draw all displayed signs independently and uniformly from \(\{-1,+1\}\). If \(T\) is even, let \(m_T=(T-2)/2\) and \(Z=(A_1,\ldots,A_{m_T},B,-A_{m_T},\ldots,-A_1)\). If \(T\) is odd, let \(m_T=(T-3)/2\) and \(Z=(A_1,\ldots,A_{m_T},B,C,-A_{m_T},\ldots,-A_1)\). Draw \(X_1\) independently and set \(X_{t+1}=X_tZ_t\); \(D_T^{\mathrm{mir}}\) is the resulting law of \(X\).

definitions.name: Legal stationary assignment laws
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak D_{\infty}=\{P_{\infty}\in\Delta(\{-1,+1\}^{\mathbb Z}):P_{\infty}\ \text{is shift invariant},\ P_{\infty}(B)=P_{\infty}(-B)\ \text{for every }B,\ \mathbb E_{P_{\infty}}[X_0^{\infty}X_h^{\infty}]=0\ \text{for every }h\ne0\}\).

definitions.name: Random-phase affine Boolean Golay-block law
definitions.construction: Let \(L=2^p\). In each block draw \(\alpha\in\mathbb F_2^p\) and \(\sigma\in\{-1,+1\}\) uniformly and independently, set \(\phi_L(j)=\sum_{r=0}^{p-2}j_rj_{r+1}\pmod 2\) for the binary digits \((j_0,\ldots,j_{p-1})\) of \(j\), and set \(W_j=\sigma(-1)^{\phi_L(j)+\sum_{r=0}^{p-1}\alpha_rj_r}\). Concatenate independent blocks in both directions and shift the origin by an independent uniform phase in \(\{0,\ldots,L-1\}\); the resulting law is \(D_L^{\mathrm G}\).

definitions.name: Coefficient-level fourth-moment tensor
definitions.construction: For a finite multiset \(J\subseteq\{0,\ldots,L-1\}\), let \(\kappa_L(J)=0\) if \(|J|\) is odd and \(\kappa_L(J)=\mathbf 1\{\bigoplus_{j\in J}j=0\}(-1)^{\sum_{j\in J}\phi_L(j)}\) if \(|J|\) is even. For integers \(t_1,\ldots,t_4\), put \(b_p(t)=\lfloor(t+p)/L\rfloor\), \(j_p(t)=(t+p)\bmod L\), and \(\Theta_L(t_1,t_2,t_3,t_4)=L^{-1}\sum_{p=0}^{L-1}\prod_b\kappa_L(\{j_p(t_r):b_p(t_r)=b\})\).

definitions.name: Lag-sum and boundary covariance objects
definitions.construction: \(C_{T,h}(x)=\sum_{t=1}^{T-h}x_tx_{t+h}\) for \(1\le h\le d\), \(M_L=\mathbb E[C_L(W)C_L(W)^{\top}]\) under one random affine Boolean block \(W\), \(H_d=\operatorname{Diag}(1,\ldots,d)\), and \((D_q)_{\ell,h}=q_{\ell-h}\mathbf 1\{\ell\ge h\}+q_{\ell+h}\mathbf 1\{\ell+h<K\}\).

definitions.name: Lag-four realizability handle
definitions.construction: Project the genuine binary moment polytope generated by \(\Phi_T(X)\Phi_T(X)^{\top}\) onto the Toeplitz lag coordinates used by \(u_T\), retain every zero-prehistory boundary coordinate, and seek necessity by parity-polynomial separation together with sufficiency by sign-orbit mixture recovery.

statements.statement: For every \(D\in\mathfrak D_T\), \(\widehat\tau-\tau=u_T(X)^{\top}g+v_T(X)^{\top}e\), \(\mathbb E_D[u_Tv_T^{\top}]=0\), \(\mathbb E_D[v_Tv_T^{\top}]=F_{T,q}F_{T,q}^{\top}\), and \(\mathcal R_T(D)=\max\{T R_g^2\lambda_{\max}(\mathbb E_D[u_Tu_T^{\top}]),\ T^2R_e^2\|F_{T,q}\|_{\mathrm{op}}^2\}\).
statements.justification: This equality exposes fourth assignment moments as the only optimizable signal block while preserving the design-invariant disturbance floor.
statements.gap: Liang and Recht calculate the corresponding blocks under independent Rademacher assignment; they do not optimize the fourth-moment block over correlated pairwise-orthogonal laws.
statements.consumer: It converts the causal design problem into a finite orbit SDP and supplies the lower noise-floor certificate for both main theorems.

statements.statement: For every \(T\ge4\), \(D_T^{\mathrm{mir}}\in\mathfrak D_T\), \(\mathbb E_{D_T^{\mathrm{mir}}}[S_T^2]=a_T\), and every nonempty consecutive product of the edge signs \(Z\) has mean zero. Moreover, the pointwise lower certificates are \(S_T^2\ge1\) when \(T\) is even and \(S_T^2\ge2-2(-1)^{(T-1)/2}X_1X_T\) when \(T\) is odd.
statements.justification: The lemma is the matching primal construction and parity dual certificate, including the class-membership proof that cannot be assumed.
statements.gap: Prior parity geometry concerns second-moment slices; no checked paper gives this edge-product law satisfying all path pair moments.
statements.consumer: It certifies an implementable minimax N-of-1 assignment for every horizon without fixed treatment counts.

statements.statement: The displayed \(T=4\) table satisfies \(S_4=B\) row by row, \(\mathbb E_{D_4^{\mathrm{mir}}}[XX^{\top}]=I_4\), and \(\mathbb E_{D_4^{\mathrm{mir}}}[S_4^2]=1\); hence it gives a direct finite audit of \(D_4^{\mathrm{mir}}\in\mathfrak D_4\) and the even-horizon bound.
statements.justification: The complete support table exposes every probability, path, edge sum, and pairwise-moment check in the smallest nontrivial horizon.
statements.gap: Neither covariance relaxations nor independent-toggling calculations exhibit a correlated binary law whose full path-pair moment matrix and parity value can be inspected row by row.
statements.consumer: It is a reproducible unit test for implementations of the mirrored randomizer and for the \(T=4\) parity certificate.

statements.statement: If \(K=2\), \(q=(1,0)^{\top}\), and \(T\ge4\), then \(V_{T,2}(q;R_g,R_e)=\max\{R_e^2,a_T R_g^2/T\}\). A law \(D\in\mathfrak D_T\) is minimax if and only if \(\mathbb E_D[S_T^2]\le\max\{a_T,r_T\}\). When \(r_T\le a_T\), this is equality and the carryover-minimizing laws are exactly those supported on \(S_T\in\{-1,1\}\) for even \(T\) and on \(S_T\in\{-2,0,2\}\) for odd \(T\).
statements.justification: This is the exact finite-horizon optimal design and complete optimizer face, including the parity discontinuity invisible to covariance-based design.
statements.gap: Liang and Recht fix independent assignment. Thiyageswaran et al. (2026), arXiv:2601.17145v1, Appendix F.3, pp. 31--32, derive in Example 10 a Rademacher objective proportional to \((x^{\top}Lx)^2\); the immediately following paragraph relaxes \(x\) to a Gaussian vector and obtains \(\mathbb E[(x^{\top}Lx)^2]=\operatorname{Tr}(LX)^2+2\operatorname{Tr}((LX)^2)\) by Isserlis's identity. That relaxation neither characterizes realizable temporal fourth moments nor yields the exact all-law fixed-path minimax value and optimizer face.
statements.consumer: A future binary N-of-1 trial with one carryover lag can select a certified assignment law and know exactly when independent toggling wastes MSE.

statements.statement: If \(K=2\), \(q=(1,0)^{\top}\), and \(T\ge4\), then \(D_T^{\mathrm{iid}}\in\mathfrak D_T\), \(\mathbb E_{D_T^{\mathrm{iid}}}[S_T^2]=T-1\), and \(\mathcal R_T(D_T^{\mathrm{iid}})=\max\{R_e^2,(T-1)R_g^2/T\}\). Therefore independent Rademacher assignment is minimax if and only if \(R_e^2/R_g^2\ge(T-1)/T\); below this threshold its excess normalized MSE is \((T-1)R_g^2/T-\max\{R_e^2,a_TR_g^2/T\}>0\).
statements.justification: The corollary gives the exact signal-to-disturbance frontier at which unrestricted fourth-order design ceases to improve on independent toggling.
statements.gap: Guo and Liang obtain asymptotic iid optimality for an E-optimal OLS information criterion within structured switching families; this finite threshold instead concerns worst-case fixed-path MSE of the displayed unbiased moment estimator over every pairwise-orthogonal law.
statements.consumer: A trial designer can decide from \(R_e^2/R_g^2\) whether iid toggling is certified or whether the mirrored law yields a strict finite-horizon gain.

statements.statement: For every \(T\ge4\), \(\mathfrak D_T^{\mathrm{RS}}\cap\mathfrak D_T=\{D_T^{\mathrm{iid}}\}\subsetneq\mathfrak D_T\), and \(D_T^{\mathrm{mir}}\in\mathfrak D_T\setminus\mathfrak D_T^{\mathrm{RS}}\). If \(K=2\), \(q=(1,0)^{\top}\), and \(R_e^2/R_g^2<(T-1)/T\), no Guo--Liang random-switch law that also satisfies global sign symmetry and pairwise orthogonality attains the finite-horizon parity optimum, whereas \(D_T^{\mathrm{mir}}\) does. This separation is for the fixed-path worst-case MSE of \(\widehat\tau\); it does not compare numerical values with Guo and Liang's asymptotic E-optimal OLS criterion.
statements.justification: The theorem makes the feasible-class relation and the exact finite regime of nonattainment by the published random-switch family auditable.
statements.gap: Guo and Liang restrict their large-horizon E-optimal OLS analysis to stationary homogeneous Markov switching, whereas the parity optimizer uses dependence outside that family and is evaluated by fixed-path moment-estimator MSE.
statements.consumer: It tells an N-of-1 designer when enlarging the legal assignment search beyond homogeneous random-switch laws is necessary to realize the exact parity gain.

statements.statement: Under \(D_L^{\mathrm G}\), \(\mathbb E[X_s^{\infty}]=0\), \(\mathbb E[X_s^{\infty}X_t^{\infty}]=\mathbf 1\{s=t\}\), and \(\mathbb E[X_{t_1}^{\infty}X_{t_2}^{\infty}X_{t_3}^{\infty}X_{t_4}^{\infty}]=\Theta_L(t_1,t_2,t_3,t_4)\) for all integer indices. Every affine Boolean block \(W\) satisfies \(|C_{L,h}(W)|\le h\) for \(1\le h\le d<L/2\), so \(\operatorname{tr}(M_L+H_d)\le\sum_{h=1}^{d}(h^2+h)\). Moreover, \(T^{-1}\mathbb E[C_T(X^{\infty})C_T(X^{\infty})^{\top}]\to(M_L+H_d)/L\). Equivalently, \(B\) complete blocks have lag-sum covariance \(B M_L+(B-1)H_d\), and all covariances between internal and boundary lag sums vanish.
statements.justification: This is the coefficient-level fourth-moment and endpoint certificate needed to transfer a classical code into a one-path causal randomization law.
statements.gap: Golay and Davis--Jedwab prove complementary autocorrelation identities, and Mazáč proves infinite Rudin--Shapiro correlation recurrences; none supplies this independent-block random-phase tensor and boundary covariance.
statements.consumer: The certificate makes the design auditable and yields exact risk for the actual zero-prehistory moment estimator rather than a circular surrogate.

statements.statement: The \(L=8\) primitive character average in the displayed table yields \(\mathbb E[W_{j_1}\cdots W_{j_m}]=0\) for odd \(m\) and \(\mathbb E[W_{j_1}\cdots W_{j_m}]=\mathbf 1\{\bigoplus_rj_r=0\}(-1)^{\sum_r\phi_8(j_r)}\) for even \(m\). In particular, \(\mathbb E[W_0W_1W_2W_3]=-1\), \(M_8=\begin{psmallmatrix}1&0&-1\\0&0&0\\-1&0&5\end{psmallmatrix}\) for \(d=3\), and \(M_8+H_3=\begin{psmallmatrix}2&0&-1\\0&2&0\\-1&0&8\end{psmallmatrix}\).
statements.justification: This worked block computes the fourth character tensor and lag-sum covariance from all eight affine masks rather than appealing only to a named Golay identity.
statements.gap: Classical complementarity gives paired autocorrelation cancellation, whereas the table records the single randomized block's coefficient-level fourth moments and the exact covariance needed by the causal risk.
statements.consumer: It is the small-block audit for the stationary construction and isolates sign, bit-order, and endpoint conventions before the general proof.

statements.statement: For fixed \(K\) and \(q\), \(u_T(X)=T^{-1}D_qC_T(X)+\rho_T(X)\), where \(\sup_X\|\rho_T(X)\|_2=O_{K,q}(T^{-1})\). Under \(D_L^{\mathrm G}\), the normalized contribution of \(\rho_T\) and its covariance with \(D_qC_T(X^{\infty})/T\) vanish. Also \(T\|F_{T,q}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\to N_q\).
statements.justification: The lemma closes the load-bearing difference between circular code identities and the estimator's exact finite linear-convolution denominators.
statements.gap: Liang and Recht compare linear and circular convolutions asymptotically under independent assignment, but do not establish this coefficient-level remainder for the randomized block law.
statements.consumer: It validates using finite Golay blocks in a trial that begins from zero prehistory rather than from an artificial periodic steady state.

statements.statement: For every fixed \(K\ge2\), \(q\in\mathbb R^K\), and positive \(R_g,R_e\), \(\lim_{T\to\infty}V_{T,K}(q;R_g,R_e)=V_{\infty,K}(q;R_g,R_e)=R_e^2N_q^2\). For every power of two \(L\ge2d\), \(D_L^{\mathrm G}\in\mathfrak D_{\infty}\), it has at most \(2L^2\) hidden states, and \(\mathcal R_{\infty,K}(D_L^{\mathrm G})=\max\{R_e^2N_q^2,(R_g^2/L)\lambda_{\max}(D_q(M_L+H_d)D_q^{\top})\}\). Consequently, if \(L\ge\max\{2d,B_KR_g^2/R_e^2\}\), then \(\mathcal R_{\infty,K}(D_L^{\mathrm G})=R_e^2N_q^2\).
statements.justification: This theorem identifies the global stationary efficiency frontier and supplies a finite-state optimal randomization with a matching spectral lower bound.
statements.gap: Tellambura, Guo, and Barton use two deterministic complementary inputs for an information criterion; no checked result proves one-path design-based minimax MSE or equality with the finite-horizon limit.
statements.consumer: It gives an implementable long-horizon binary assignment law for individualized impulse-response experiments when treatment counts may remain random.

statements.statement: For arbitrary finite \(T,K,q\), can the projection of \(\{\mathbb E_D[\Phi_T\Phi_T^{\top}]:D\in\mathfrak D_T\}\) relevant to \(\mathbb E_D[u_Tu_T^{\top}]\) be characterized by a lag-sized necessary-and-sufficient family of parity and positivity inequalities with explicit sign-orbit recovery, and can that characterization yield a quantitative finite-horizon bound \(|V_{T,K}-R_e^2N_q^2|\le c(K,q,R_g,R_e)/T\)?
statements.justification: This exposes the genuinely unresolved general-order content instead of presenting a generic orbit SDP as a closed-form solution.
statements.gap: Bandeira and Kunisky characterize degree-four pseudomoments rather than genuine binary-law moments, and Manchester's input-design lift has an approximation gap.
statements.consumer: A lag-sized certificate would permit exact finite-sample design optimization for multi-lag N-of-1 targets without enumerating \(2^T\) paths.

sampling_model.design: One binary treatment path is drawn from a chosen \(D\in\mathfrak D_T\); the assignment is the only randomness.
sampling_model.units: A single fixed experimental unit observed at \(T\) ordered periods.
sampling_model.treatment: \(X_t\in\{-1,+1\}\), with random treatment counts and zero prehistory.
sampling_model.overlap: Global sign symmetry and exact pairwise orthogonality replace independent assignment; no fixed-count constraint is imposed.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The fixed vectors \(g\) and \(e\) range jointly over \(\mathcal H_T\); no nuisance law, plug-in variance, or Wald approximation is used.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Section 2.2, equation (6) and the immediately following display analyze the method-of-moments estimator as quadratic chaos under independent Rademacher toggling; Section 6 states that the paper only considers random toggling at each time step.
Definition 3.6 defines the asymptotic OLS objective, Definition 4.1 defines stationary homogeneous random-switch designs, and Theorem 4.6 sends the robust-design minimizers to \((1/2,1/2)\).
The paper states, \(\text{we cast the experimental design problem as a minimax discrete robust optimization problem}\).
For a complementary pair, the sum of the two autocorrelation series vanishes away from the center term.
Theorem 3 proves that the displayed affine quadratic Boolean sequences form a Golay complementary pair.
The paper states that eigenvalues of autocorrelation matrices of a complementary pair sum to a known constant.
The paper states that all odd-point balanced Rudin--Shapiro correlations vanish and even-point correlations reduce to one number.
The paper states that its main result is a necessary and sufficient Gramian condition for degree-four generalized-elliptope membership.
The main result gives a convex-relaxation upper bound accurate to within \(2/\pi\) of the amplitude-constrained optimum.

In arXiv:2601.17145v1, Appendix F.3, pp. 31--32, Example 10 derives a Rademacher objective proportional to \((x^{\top}Lx)^2\), and the immediately following paragraph relaxes \(x\) to a Gaussian vector and gives \(\mathbb E[(x^{\top}Lx)^2]=\operatorname{Tr}(LX)^2+2\operatorname{Tr}((LX)^2)\) by Isserlis's identity.

tldr: For a single fixed impulse-response path, pairwise-orthogonal binary designs have identical second moments but different fourth-order risk for the unbiased moment estimator. The project derives the exact all-horizon minimax MSE and complete optimizer face when \(K=2\), including an even--odd parity gap, mirrored-edge-sign attaining laws, a fully displayed \(T=4\) audit, the exact threshold for iid optimality, and a strict feasible-class separation showing when stationary homogeneous random-switch laws cannot realize the parity optimum. It then constructs a stationary finite-state randomized Golay-block law, verifies the primitive \(L=8\) fourth tensor, proves the general boundary tensor, and shows that for every fixed \(K\) and \(q\) it attains the spectral disturbance floor shared by the finite-horizon and stationary limits.

project_justification.gap: Existing N-of-1 inference fixes independent toggling, current temporal optimal-design theory restricts assignment to structured Markov families and an OLS criterion, and recent network-design work relaxes an explicit fourth-order Rademacher objective to Gaussian covariance optimization. None characterizes the exact realizable fourth moments controlling fixed-path design-based MSE for one temporal path.
project_justification.niche: The open niche is global optimal randomization for an already-identified causal moment under fixed finite-population potential outcomes, with assignment-law fourth moments as the design variable and an exact minimax certificate as the deliverable.
project_justification.fill: The parity theorem solves the first nontrivial finite problem exactly, yields the finite iid-optimality threshold, and isolates the legal portion of the published random-switch family as iid alone, while the Golay-block theorem supplies a finite-state stationary optimizer, primitive \(T=4\) and \(L=8\) audits, a complete tensor certificate, and the spectral lower bound that certifies global asymptotic optimality.

related_work: Liang and Recht (2025), Section 2.2, equation (6), the immediately following quadratic-chaos display, Appendix A.1, and Section 6 define the same linear causal estimands and moment estimator, analyze it under independent Rademacher toggling, and leave deliberate assignment design open; the strict comparison here optimizes that fourth-order term over all legal laws. Guo and Liang (2026), Definition 3.6, define the asymptotic OLS objective; Definition 4.1 defines stationary homogeneous random-switch designs; and Theorem 4.6 sends robust-design minimizers to \((1/2,1/2)\). The iid-threshold corollary instead gives an exact finite-horizon frontier for fixed-path worst-case MSE of the unbiased moment estimator over the unrestricted pairwise-orthogonal class, and the class-separation theorem proves that the intersection of their random-switch family with the legal class is the iid law alone and cannot attain the parity optimum below that threshold. These are distinct criteria, so the class comparison does not identify their OLS objective with the fixed-path moment-estimator MSE. Thiyageswaran et al. (2026), arXiv:2601.17145v1, Appendix F.3, pp. 31--32, derive in Example 10 a Rademacher objective proportional to \((x^{\top}Lx)^2\); the immediately following paragraph relaxes \(x\) to a Gaussian vector and obtains \(\mathbb E[(x^{\top}Lx)^2]=\operatorname{Tr}(LX)^2+2\operatorname{Tr}((LX)^2)\) by Isserlis's identity. That calculation establishes the relevance of fourth-order design but does not subsume this kernel: Gaussian fourth moments need not be realizable by a binary temporal law, the network GATE and Horvitz--Thompson criterion differ from the one-path impulse-response moment-estimator MSE, and it supplies neither zero-prehistory boundary normalization nor an exact parity or stationary minimax certificate. Bojinov, Simchi-Levi, and Zhao (2023), Theorem 3.7, solve regular-switchback minimax design under bounded carryover potential outcomes through adversary reduction and continuous relaxation; their design and adversary classes differ. Golay (1961) and Davis and Jedwab (1999), Theorem 3, supply the classical complementary sequence construction used inside the stationary law. Tellambura, Guo, and Barton (1998), equations (8)--(10), connect complementary deterministic training pairs to impulse-response information matrices, but do not produce one causal randomization path or its fourth tensor. Mazáč (2024), Proposition 4.2 and Section 6, supplies recursive machinery for higher Rudin--Shapiro correlations. Bandeira and Kunisky (2018), Theorems 2.15 and 2.17 and Section 4.3, and Manchester (2010), the main \(2/\pi\) approximation theorem, supply degree-four pseudomoment geometry and time-domain SDP relaxation; both are methodological inputs rather than exact results for the realizable causal design class.
technical_internal_limitation: Exact enumeration validates the proposed parity and block identities only at the stated small horizons and block lengths; those computations are evidence, not proofs. The load-bearing proof obligations are the random-phase endpoint tensor, the zero-prehistory denominator remainder, and the finite-state membership statement. The joint ellipsoid alone permits a disturbance spike for which \(\sqrt T(\widehat\tau-\tau)\) remains two-point, so no uniform Wald conclusion is claimed.
honest_scope: The theorems concern the displayed unbiased moment estimator, not joint minimaxity over all estimators. Treatment counts are random: exact fixed balance is incompatible with pairwise orthogonality because it would force both \(\mathbb E(\sum_tX_t)^2=0\) and \(\mathbb E(\sum_tX_t)^2=T\). The result is binary and does not cover the third arm in SAMSON. Gaussian or covariance relaxations of fourth-order objectives do not certify membership in the genuine binary temporal moment body. As a sanity reduction, under independent Rademacher assignment and \(K=2\), \(\mathbb E S_T^2=T-1\), recovering the anchor's independent quadratic-chaos variance; at \(T=4\), the displayed optimal law instead has \(\mathbb E S_T^2=1\). The exact general finite-\(K\) realizable lag-four body and an explicit \(T^{-1}\) boundary rate remain open.

seed_details.anchor_opened: The Introduction, Section 2.2, equation (6), the immediately following quadratic-chaos display, Appendix A.1, and Section 6 were read. novelty_justification: The closest estimator paper, Liang and Recht (2025), Section 2.2, equation (6), and the immediately following display fix independent toggling for the same method-of-moments estimator. The closest temporal design paper, Guo and Liang (2026), Definition 3.6 defines the asymptotic OLS objective, Definition 4.1 defines stationary homogeneous random-switch designs, and Theorem 4.6 sends robust-design minimizers to \((1/2,1/2)\). The class-separation theorem proves that this family's intersection with the legal pairwise-orthogonal class is iid alone and cannot attain the finite parity optimum when \(R_e^2/R_g^2<(T-1)/T\), without equating the two papers' criteria. Thiyageswaran et al. (2026), arXiv:2601.17145v1, Appendix F.3, pp. 31--32, derive in Example 10 a Rademacher objective proportional to \((x^{\top}Lx)^2\); the immediately following paragraph relaxes \(x\) to a Gaussian vector and gives \(\mathbb E[(x^{\top}Lx)^2]=\operatorname{Tr}(LX)^2+2\operatorname{Tr}((LX)^2)\) by Isserlis's identity. The exact delta is optimization over every globally sign-symmetric pairwise-orthogonal binary law for fixed-path moment-estimator MSE, where Gaussian covariance feasibility does not characterize realizable temporal fourth moments. The finite theorem adds an all-horizon parity-dependent value, complete optimizer face, exact iid-optimality threshold, and restricted-class nonrepresentability result. The stationary theorem adds a one-path randomized lift of classical Golay codes, its exact fourth tensor and boundary covariance, and equality between finite-horizon and stationary minimax limits. Classical Golay and Davis--Jedwab sequence construction is explicitly treated as imported method, not novelty.
